title: Corey's Diels–Alder: a ketene equivalent
subtitle: 2-Chloroacrylonitrile adds to a substituted cyclopentadiene and builds the bicyclic skeleton

reactants.caption: 5-(methoxymethyl)cyclopenta-1,3-diene + 2-chloroacrylonitrile
reactants.learnerPrompt: Draw the Diels–Alder reaction that joins the diene to the C=C of 2-chloroacrylonitrile.
hintTiers: A Diels–Alder reaction is one concerted step: three curly arrows go round a six-membered ring of atoms, the four carbons of the diene and the two carbons of the dienophile's C=C.

Each end of the diene bonds to one carbon of the dienophile, and the diene's middle bond becomes the new C=C. The ring carbon carrying the CH₂OMe group takes no part: it ends up as the one-carbon bridge.

Dienophile C=C π bond → new bond from its CH₂ carbon to one end of the diene; the diene π bond at that end → a π bond across the diene's middle; the other diene π bond → new bond from its end carbon to the carbon carrying Cl and CN.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The ring carbon carrying the CH₂OMe group is sp³: it has no π electrons and cannot form a new bond here. The diene's ends are the two carbons of the C=C bonds next to it.
New bonds form at the ends of the diene, not at its middle carbons. The middle bond of the diene becomes the new C=C.
The C≡N group only pulls electron density out of the C=C; the C=C is the dienophile. It will be used later as a handle to unmask a ketone.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the dienophile's π bond makes the first new bond. Now push the diene's electrons round the ring: two more arrows.

adduct.caption: the bicyclo[2.2.1]heptene: 2-chloro-7-(methoxymethyl)bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-5-ene-2-carbonitrile, as a mixture of epimers at the carbon carrying Cl and CN

steps.explanationAfterStep: One concerted [4+2] cycloaddition: two new σ bonds and a new C=C between the diene's middle carbons. The cyclopentadiene ring becomes a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptene, and the CH₂OMe carbon becomes its one-carbon bridge. The dienophile approaches the face of the diene away from the CH₂OMe group, so that group ends up leaning over the new C=C, away from the new two-carbon bridge (not checked by the app yet).

mechanismSummary: Corey's prostaglandin synthesis starts by building a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptene. 5-(Methoxymethyl)cyclopentadiene (kept cold, or 1,5-hydrogen shifts move the substituent onto the diene) reacts with 2-chloroacrylonitrile in one concerted Diels–Alder step. Ketene itself does [2+2] cycloadditions, not Diels–Alder reactions, so the chloronitrile stands in for it: its carbon carrying Cl and CN will later become a ketone C=O, so it is a 'ketene equivalent'. Stereochemistry (explained, not yet checked by the app): the dienophile adds to the face of the diene away from the CH₂OMe group, which fixes the relative configuration of three of the five ring carbons of the final cyclopentane. The Cl and CN groups end up as a mixture of exo and endo epimers, which does not matter, because that carbon becomes the ketone. A copper(II) tetrafluoroborate catalyst speeds up the reaction as a Lewis acid on the nitrile; it is not drawn.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 34 (Diels–Alder reactions; ketene equivalents)
E. J. Corey, N. M. Weinshenker, T. K. Schaaf and W. Huber, Stereo-controlled synthesis of dl-prostaglandins F2α and E2, J. Am. Chem. Soc., 1969, 91, 5675–5677
